entities.name: Isaurian dynasty
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Isaurian Dynasty (717-802 CE), also known as the Syrian Dynasty, founded by Leo III (the Isaurian) — who halted the Arab Muslim siege of Constantinople in 717-718 CE in one of history's most consequential defensive battles — is best known for inaugurating the Byzantine Iconoclasm (726-787 CE, with a second phase 815-843 CE), the violent theological and political controversy over the veneration of religious images that divided the Byzantine Empire, alienated the papacy, and contributed to the rupture between Eastern and Western Christianity that eventually became the Great Schism.

Leo III's 717-718 defense of Constantinople was a genuinely decisive moment: an Arab Umayyad fleet and army besieged the city for over a year; Leo used Greek fire to destroy the Arab fleet and allied with Bulgarian forces to defeat the land army. The Arab failure at Constantinople (coupled with the Frankish defeat of the Arab advance at the Battle of Tours/Poitiers in 732) effectively halted the Arab expansion into Europe, preserving Byzantine civilization and European Christendom.

Leo III's iconoclasm (726-730, intensified 730) — the theological position that the veneration of religious images was idolatry forbidden by the Second Commandment — created the first major Byzantine theological conflict since the Christological controversies. The iconoclasm persecuted icon venerators, destroyed images, alienated Pope Gregory III (who condemned it in 731), and forced a fundamental reevaluation of Christian visual culture. The First Council of Nicaea (787 CE) under Empress Irene (Isaurian dynasty's final ruler) restored icon veneration, but the controversy had permanently damaged East-West church relations.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Isaurian Dynasty — halting the Arab siege of Constantinople (717-718) in one of history's most consequential defensive victories, inaugurating the Iconoclasm controversy that helped cause the Great Schism, and reshaping Byzantine theology and East-West relations — is one of the most historically pivotal Byzantine dynasties.
